question: What is the primary goal of screening pregnant women for home delivery?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any further antenatal visits
options.B: To separate low-risk mothers from those who need hospital care
options.C: To calculate the exact date and hour labor will begin
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing baby clothes

explanation: Screening helps identify who can safely give birth at home and who requires a facility with advanced medical help. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why must a nurse repeat risk assessments throughout the entire pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy conditions and risks can change as the weeks progress
options.B: Mothers tend to forget their medical history if not asked often
options.C: Blood pressure and weight never stay stable for more than a month
options.D: Hospital guidelines require paperwork to be filled out weekly

explanation: A woman who starts her pregnancy healthy can develop complications like high blood pressure later on. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is a major benefit of continuous antenatal risk assessment?

options.A: Complete prevention of all natural labor pains
options.B: Early detection of potential complications before labor starts
options.C: Guaranteeing that the baby will be born on a specific day
options.D: Removing the need for traditional birth attendants entirely

explanation: Catching warning signs early allows the healthcare team to act before a minor issue becomes an emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h2)

question: How does discussing risk assessment openly help the pregnant mother?

options.A: It empowers her to understand danger signs and join healthcare decisions
options.B: It frightens her enough to ensure she obeys every hospital rule
options.C: It stops her from asking questions during labor
options.D: It proves to her family that nurses know everything about birth

explanation: Open communication helps the mother recognize when something is wrong and trust the care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which baby position is required for a planned home delivery to be considered safe?
explanation: A head-first presentation is essential for a safe vaginal birth, especially outside of a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following women is the best candidate for a planned home delivery?

options.A: A 28-year-old with two normal past births, currently at 39 weeks with a head-first baby
options.B: A mother who experienced a severe heavy bleed after her last delivery
options.C: A 40-year-old carrying twins at 34 weeks who has severe chronic high blood pressure
options.D: A first-time mother whose baby is currently lying completely sideways in the womb

explanation: This mother has a term, single, head-first baby and a history of normal births, fitting all low-risk criteria. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is a previous classical cesarean section a strong contraindication for home delivery?

options.A: The baby will automatically be born too early
options.B: It causes the mother to lose her voice during contractions
options.C: Stitches from the old operation will make the baby cold
options.D: There is a high risk of uterine rupture during labor

explanation: A scarred uterus can tear open under the pressure of strong contractions, which is a life-threatening emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which condition makes a home birth unsafe because of the high chance of bleeding and delivery complications?
explanation: Multiple gestations carry a high risk of abnormal positioning and severe bleeding after birth, requiring hospital standby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of performing Leopold's maneuvers during an antenatal visit?

options.A: To check if the mother has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine fetal position, size, and presentation
options.C: To measure the exact amount of blood in the body
options.D: To find out when the baby will start walking

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers use gentle hand movements on the abdomen to feel how the baby is lying. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why is routine urinalysis important during pregnancy checkups?

options.A: It checks for protein and sugar, which show kidney stress or diabetes
options.B: It measures the heartbeat of the unborn baby
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact weight of the placenta
options.D: It proves whether the mother is eating enough vegetables

explanation: Protein in urine can point to pre-eclampsia, while sugar can point to diabetes, both needing close management. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why must a nurse evaluate the road conditions and distance to the hospital for a home birth?

options.A: To calculate how much fuel the nurse's car will burn
options.B: To find the cheapest taxi fare for the family
options.C: To decide if the baby will be born during the day or night
options.D: To plan a safe and fast emergency transfer if complications happen

explanation: If labor goes wrong, bad roads or long distances can delay life-saving hospital care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which home feature is NOT necessary to ensure a safe and hygienic delivery space?

options.A: A clean space for the birth
options.B: A large television set for entertainment

explanation: A television is not needed for clinical safety, whereas water, lighting, and cleanliness are essential. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of an emergency preparedness plan in home births?

options.A: To make sure the birth happens without any pain medication
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching a hospital during complications
options.C: To guarantee that the birth takes less than two hours
options.D: To collect gifts from neighbors before the baby arrives

explanation: Having transport, money, and a destination ready saves precious time when an emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that means a home birth must be stopped and transferred immediately?

options.B: Swelling of the fingers in hot weather

explanation: Heavy bleeding is a sign of a dangerous obstetric emergency like placental abruption or previa, needing urgent hospital care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h7)

question: What does 'informed consent' mean when planning a home delivery?

options.A: The doctor signs a paper without telling the mother anything
options.B: The family understands the risks and benefits and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The government forces every woman to give birth at home
options.D: The traditional birth attendant makes all decisions for the family

explanation: Informed consent requires that patients are fully aware of what they are choosing and agree of their own free will. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)

question: Why is accurate documentation of the screening process vital on the antenatal card?

options.A: It stops the mother from changing her mind about her due date
options.B: It replaces the need to talk to the family during labor
options.C: It ensures the nurse gets a higher salary each month
options.D: It provides continuity of care if another provider takes over

explanation: Written records allow any healthcare worker to quickly see the patient's risk status and history in an emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)
